question.worked_solution:
First, we find the first-order derivative ${f}_{x}(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{x}(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡(y+z)) \\  & =2x\operatorname{ln}⁡(y+z)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find ${f}_{xy}(x,y,z)$ by differentiating ${f}_{x}(x,y,z)$ with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{xy}(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({f}_{x}(x,y,z)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(2x\operatorname{ln}⁡(y+z)) \\  & =2x\cdot \frac{1}{y+z} \\  & =\frac{2x}{y+z}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find ${f}_{xyz}(x,y,z)$ by differentiating ${f}_{xy}(x,y,z)$ with respect to $z:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{xyz}(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂z}({f}_{xy}(x,y,z)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂z}(\frac{2x}{y+z}) \\  & =2x\cdot \frac{∂}{∂z}(\frac{1}{y+z}) \\  & =2x\cdot (-\frac{1}{(y+z)^{2}}) \\  & =-\frac{2x}{(y+z)^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate ${f}_{xyz}(x,y,z)$ at $(-5,2,3):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{xyz}(-5,2,3) & =-\frac{2(-5)}{(2+3)^{2}}=\frac{2}{5}\end{aligned}
$$
